name: Kepler Space Telescope

crew.cmp: NASA Ames / Ball Aerospace Flight Ops

landing.label: Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Drift Orbit (Cygnus / Lyra Field)

terrain.note: Silent heliocentric drift orbit 150 million km from Earth, trailing behind our planet's orbit

keyDiscovery: Discovered 2,662 confirmed alien planets beyond our Solar System, proving mathematically that planets outnumber stars in the Milky Way.
missionLegacy: Revolutionized astronomy and astrobiology by finding the first Earth-size habitable zone worlds (Kepler-186f, Kepler-452b), answering humanity's oldest question: 'Are we alone?'

objects.name: 0.95-Meter Schmidt Photometer
objects.description: 0.95-meter aperture Schmidt telescope with a 1.4-meter primary mirror focusing light onto a curved focal plane array of 42 CCDs totaling 95 megapixels.
objects.source: NASA Ames Research Center / Ball Aerospace
objects.scienceDiscovery: Measured the ultra-tiny dip in starlight (down to 10 parts per million) caused by an exoplanet transiting in front of its host star.
objects.legacy: The most prolific planet-finding instrument ever constructed in human history.
objects.firstPerson: I am the Kepler Space Telescope. For nine years, my giant eye stared unblinkingly at 150,000 stars in Cygnus and Lyra.

objects.name: Curved Carbon-Fiber Sunshade Baffle
objects.description: Slanted carbon-fiber composite sunshade baffle lined with specular coatings, keeping direct sunlight from entering the telescope optics.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Provided cryogenic thermal stability for the telescope focal plane without requiring consumable coolant.
objects.legacy: Enabled continuous photometric observations unaffected by stray light glare.
objects.firstPerson: Like a visor over my eye, my black carbon hood shielded my sensitive cameras from the blinding rays of the Sun.

objects.name: Reaction Wheel Stabilization Assembly
objects.description: Four precision momentum wheels used to stabilize the telescope pointing to micro-arcsecond accuracy, later ingeniously balanced using solar radiation pressure in the K2 mission.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Engineers pioneered solar radiation pressure pointing after two wheels failed, resurrecting the spacecraft to discover hundreds more planets in the K2 mission.
objects.legacy: One of the greatest salvage operations in robotic spaceflight history.
objects.firstPerson: When two of my spinning gyro wheels seized, Earth engineers used the gentle push of sunlight on my hull to balance me like a tightrope walker.

objects.name: Curved Body-Mounted Solar Panels
objects.description: Body-mounted curved silicon solar panels generating 1,100 W, designed with integral thermal radiators to dump electronic heat into space.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Eliminated mechanical solar array drive vibration, giving Kepler the ultra-stable platform required for transit photometry.
objects.legacy: Set the engineering standard for vibration-free space astronomy architectures.
objects.firstPerson: Curved around my back, my solar cells soaked up power silently without moving a single gear, keeping my telescope rock-steady.

objects.name: High-Gain Communications Antenna
objects.description: Gimbaled high-gain antenna dish transmitting Ka-band science data back to NASA's Deep Space Network at 4.3 Mbps.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Beamed down 678 gigabytes of uncompressed photometric light curves containing the signatures of thousands of worlds.
objects.legacy: Delivered the scientific data that established the field of exoplanetary statistics.
objects.firstPerson: Once a month, I turned my antenna toward home and sent gigabytes of starlight data, whispering the locations of distant alien worlds.

objects.name: Gold Kapton MLI Equipment Enclosure
objects.description: Multi-layer insulation (MLI) blankets composed of embossed aluminized and gold Kapton foil shielding avionics, star trackers, and hydrazine fuel tanks.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Operated down to the final drop of hydrazine propellant on 30 October 2018, having expended every gram of fuel searching for worlds.
objects.legacy: A monument to human curiosity, now drifting quietly in an Earth-trailing orbit forever.
objects.firstPerson: Wrapped in gold thermal foil, my tanks are empty and my thrusters are cold, but the thousands of worlds I found will shine forever in human history.
